newsitem.title: UK: Angola crude exports normal despite SBM repairs.
newsitem.headline: Angola crude exports normal despite SBM repairs.

text.p: Angolan Cabinda and Nemba crude exports are running as normal despite subsea repairs at the deepwater tanker mooring for Angola's main crude export terminal, Molongo, state oil company Sonangal said on Monday.

The repairs to subsea hoses at Molongo's deepwater single buoy mooring have restricted tanker loadings to 950,000-barrel cargoes from an alternative mooring in shallower water, a Sonangol official said.
Repairs started on October 20 and are scheduled to finish on November 16.
"It hasn't effected exports in the least because the old SBM can handle everything, but customers are unable to nominate VLCCs," said the official.
Molongo terminal handles exports for the 340,000 barrel a day (bpd) Cabinda crude stream and the 85,000 bpd Nemba field.
The terminal is operated by Chevron Gulf Oil Co (CABGOC) .
